description: The Global Hubs land table lists 50 dry ports and rail intermodal terminals selected for large container-handling scale. Dmitry Golubnichiy publishes CSV and Parquet files with hub and operator names, country, city-level WGS84 coordinates, TEU values and annual change where reported. The repository and Zenodo concept DOI provide free CC0 access. A freight modeller could use the locations to seed terminal nodes or compare broad inland-capacity scenarios. The README warns that values combine handled TEU, intermodal lifts and design capacity, and that reporting years differ. Therefore the rank is indicative and should not be used as an exact cross-terminal performance measure. Coordinates identify cities, not necessarily terminal entrances, and border crossings are excluded. The release is versioned in 2026, but this review did not download rows or check source reports. Related Global Hubs resources cover seaports, cargo airports and rail freight operators, each with its own DOI.
